Re-run: db=pubmed term="kaharuba" returns Count 0 with QuotedPhraseNotFound (correct); term="kahruba" returns Count 0 with QuotedPhraseNotFound (correct); term="kahruba pishti" returns Count 10, IdList 42485741, 41106206, 40163851, 39828143, 39615446, 35813362, 23723668, 22529645, 21731356, 12597554, with QueryTranslation "pishti"[All Fields] and a QuotedPhraseNotFound warning. PubMed reports the phrase as not found but does NOT return no records - it drops the quotes and returns the ten pishti records. 'Return no records at all' is false for the third term. This is the exact paragraph the record offers as its reproducibility guarantee, and it is the paragraph carrying the record's central negative claim.

audit: REJECT, but narrowly. The shape is right and almost everything verified. I re-ran every reported search and re-read every cited source; all four previous objections are genuinely fixed at root, not papered over. Three statements still fail source checking, one of them the exact failure class the brief names (an invented methodological detail). Each is a one-clause fix.

audit: BLOCKING 1 (Rule 2) - contraindications / animal-source entry, Angers 2009. The record states: 'infection attack rates below 100% meant the authors were unable to assign a definitive titer'. The paper states a different reason: 'Because the incubation times of CWD prions in antler velvet from elk 01-0306 and 03-0306 were outside the linear range of dose and incubation time (Figure 5), we were unable to assign a definitive titer. The infection attack rates <100% suggested that CWD prion titers in these 1% inocula were close to, or at, the end point of the bioassay (< 3.5 log i.c.ID50 units).' Two adjacent findings have been fused into a causal claim the study does not make. Both facts are individually true, so the fix is to state them separately: titer could not be assigned because incubation times fell outside the linear dose/incubation range, and attack rates below 100% suggested titers at or near the bioassay end point.

audit: BLOCKING - the record overclaims its own search account, and the overclaim is literally false. heavyMetals says 'Identifying every record returned:' and then identifies eleven PMIDs. The 'pishti' search returns ten records, one of which - 23723668 - is never identified anywhere in the record. I re-ran all sixteen searches through NCBI E-utilities (db=pubmed) today and every one reproduces exactly, including 'pishti' returning 42485741, 41106206, 40163851, 39828143, 39615446, 35813362, 23723668, 22529645, 21731356, 12597554. PMID 23723668 is 'Clinical evaluation of Ashokarishta, Ashwagandha Churna and Praval Pishti in the management of menopausal syndrome' (Ayu 2012), a Praval Pishti trial that reports no elemental analysis, so the substantive negative that follows ('None of these records reports a lead, mercury or arsenic measurement on Mukta Pishti') survives. What does not survive is the word 'every'. A record whose entire claim to trust is that its search reproduces cannot tell a reader it has accounted for every hit and then leave one unaccounted. Fix at the root: identify 23723668 in the enumeration alongside the others, or drop the completeness claim.

audit: BLOCKING - an absence claim about a full text the record has not read, and could not read. heavyMetals states of Balkrishna 2025: 'the paper reports no ICP-MS, no atomic absorption and no other trace-element determination', and later 'The paper states no number of batches for the test article'. The only source given for Balkrishna is the PubMed record (sources entry: pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39828143, tier 'peer-reviewed (PubMed)'), and the record itself signals elsewhere that it read Joshi's full text at PMC but says nothing of the kind here. I tried to reach the full text through doi.org, which redirects to linkinghub.elsevier.com and returns nothing; the paper is paywalled and has no PMC deposit, so neither the rebuilder nor I can confirm what the Methods section does or does not contain. This matters more than it looks: the record's headline sentence is 'No permitted source located reports a lead, mercury or arsenic measurement made on Mukta Pishti', and Balkrishna is the one preparation-specific characterization there is, so the headline negative rests on an unverified reading of an inaccessible Methods section. This is the same failure class that blocked the last pass (an assertion about a study's methods made from the abstract alone), differing only in that the last one turned out false and this one is unfalsifiable. The supportable version is small and sits right beside the unsupportable one: the abstract's METHODS lists SEM, EDX, DLS and FTIR, none of which is a quantitative trace-metal assay, and the full text was not accessible on a permitted host. Say that, and drop or similarly bound the batch-count sentence.

audit: BLOCKING (Rule 11 - a negative the record's own cited source contradicts). doseLimits states: 'No dose can be given... no permitted source states any human dose for this preparation at all.' That is false. Samal 2016 (PMC5822980), which this record cites and quotes, publishes Table 2, 'Dosage, duration and Anupana of important Ayurvedic formulations for iron deficiency anemia', whose last row reads: 'Navayasa Lauha | 250 mg twice daily | Honey | 30 days'. I read the table directly (PMC serves it as an image, https://cdn.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/blobs/c3bd/5822980/a2bfd2984ce7/AYU-37-163-g004.jpg, referenced from the article as table-wrap T2, graphic AYU-37-163-g004.jpg). The record's insufficientReason repeats the same false negative: 'Neither paper gives an ingredient list, a composition, an iron content, a dose or any safety datum for it.' A permitted source, under the exact name Navayasa Lauha, gives a dose, a vehicle and a duration. This is the same failure class the previous pass was rejected for on Sharma 2007 - converting 'I did not see it' into 'the source does not state it' - reintroduced against a different source.

audit: BLOCKING (Rule 11, and the claim 'no clinical study'). insufficientReason asserts 'No permitted source describes this preparation. There is no monograph, no elemental or heavy-metal analysis, no clinical study, no case report naming it...'. Samal 2016's Table 1 (graphic AYU-37-163-g003.jpg, https://cdn.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/blobs/c3bd/5822980/75d3465bc043/AYU-37-163-g003.jpg) reports a clinical study of the named preparation: 'Nazmul Huda Md, Daya Shankar Mishra, Singh JP. J Homeopath Ayurveda Med 2014;3:162. Randomized, nonblinded, controlled trial. 30 participants equally divided into three groups. Group 1, 2 and 3 received Starch capsule, Dhatri Lauha (250 mg) and Navayasa Lauha (250 mg) respectively, for 30 days. Hematological parameters were used to assess the results among these three groups.' with major outcomes 'Statistically significant results (P<0.05) were obtained for Dhatri Lauha and Navayasa Lauha in hematological parameters; Hb (g/dl), PCV (%), MCV (fl), MCH (pg), MCHC (g%)'. So a permitted source describes a randomised controlled trial of Navayasa Lauha with a 10-participant arm, a dose and a duration. The record's blanket 'nobody has published an analysis, a study or a monograph of it' is not supportable as written.

audit: PRIOR OBJECTION 1 FIXED AT ROOT. The rule-11 closing sentence 'None of these class-level reports tested Nityananda Rasa itself' is gone, replaced by what each report actually publishes. I confirmed each replacement clause: Mikulski's Table 3 gives nine rows over six distinct product families (Indukantham, Brihat Vatchintamani Ras, Swarna Bhasma, Saubhagya, Shulagna, Arbudari) and the paper never enumerates its 252 samples; Ciocan's implicated drug is unnamed ('One of the two drugs contained extremely high concentrations of lead and mercury'); Hore aggregates 584 remedies with no sample list.

audit: SHAPE IS CORRECT AND SHOULD NOT CHANGE. insufficientData is true, every statement carries scope 'class-level', there is no doseLimits field and insufficientReason says why, no efficacy or indication appears anywhere (Joshi's antimicrobial result and 'quite safe ... essential micronutrients' sentence, Jagtap's renal-calculi framing and Mukta Pishti's anti-ulcer framing are all correctly excluded), no study arms are spliced, pregnancy and lactation are both 'avoid' on stated developmental-neurotoxicant reasoning, and the beryllium mention is carried through to the 'undisclosed and unanalysed composition' contraindication rather than dropped. All nine source URLs are on permitted hosts, every sourceId resolves and every listed source is used. The rebuild is one transcription error away from publishable; do not restructure it.

audit: BLOCKING, Rule 2 (a value attributed to a source that the source does not state): the record says of Joshi et al. (2020) that 'Table 9 gives the maximum permissible limits it compares against ... as As 103 ng/g, Cd 0.3 microg/g, Pb 10 microg/g and Hg 1 microg/g.' I read the full text (PMC9261990). The published Table 9 markup is '10<sup>3</sup> ng/g' for As, i.e. 10^3 ng/g = 1,000 ng/g = 1 microg/g. The record has flattened a superscript into a different number roughly ten-fold low. Cd 0.3 microg/g, Pb 10 microg/g and Hg 1 microg/g are correct; only the arsenic figure is wrong. Because the sentence presents itself as reporting what Table 9 contains, it attributes to the source a limit the source does not give, and 103 ng/g is not a permissible limit stated by WHO, FDA, the API or anyone else, so a clinician or AI system citing this record would propagate an invented regulatory number. Root fix: write it as the source does, '10^3 ng/g (1,000 ng/g, i.e. 1 microg/g)'. Note that the correction slightly weakens the unit-mismatch point the passage is making, since the corrected As limit is in the same microg/g order as the other three, so the surrounding sentence should be re-checked after the fix rather than left as is; the substantive observation, that Table 8 is in weight % while Table 9 is in ng/g and microg/g, still stands.

audit: Fetched and read every cited source in full rather than relying on the rebuilder's account: PMC9728409, PMC3271539, PMC3361937, PMC6421027, PMC2755247, PMC8882783, NBK604211, NBK621375, and the NCCIH colloidal-silver page. The four defects the previous auditor required were fixed at their root. The 70 mg/kg figure now reads 'Estimated cumulative doses leading to generalized argyria in humans have been reported as low as 70 mg/kg body weight' with 'lifetime' and 'body burden' gone from both fields; the 'neither tested a silver bhasma by name' assertion is replaced with the supportable statement about sample lists; the Saper quotation now matches the printed 'One hundred ninety-three of the 230 requested medicines were received and analyzed.'; and Liu's mineral list now carries Kamksi (Al) and Sudhu (Lime).

audit: Verified verbatim and accurate: all StatPearls quotes (argyria/argyrosis as most common effects, the argyrosis definition sentence, the 55-year-old 9-year oral-mycosis case, proteinuria and damaged glomeruli, diffuse argyria at abdominal operation, blood-brain and placental barrier crossing, biliary/faecal excretion with breast milk among routes, highest concentrations in skin/liver/kidneys/cornea/gingiva, blood silver under 1 mcg/L, 'No minimum serum silver levels are consistent with early argyria', the no-antidote sentence, the 7 g intrauterine silver nitrate death, and the WHO RfD sentence carried complete including 'which is not the most sensitive toxicity endpoint'); all four NCCIH quotes; LactMed NBK621375 revision of 15 March 2026 including the undetectable-to-42 mcg/L range and the three 'Relevant published information was not found' fields; Saper's 20.7% of 193 analysed, 40.6% vs 17.1% at P=.007, and the three-metal XRF panel with silver never mentioned in the paper; Bhalla's 43 collected / 42 analysed, 'Heavy metals were detected in all formulations', 'All except one preparation had at least one metal with a concentration higher than FAO/WHO permissible limit', 35/29/6/2 above limit, 27.9% (n = 12) of 43 labelled, the eight-metal silver-free panel, and both author-stated limitations. Denominators are carried correctly throughout (Rule 12 satisfied). Inder's mouse sentences are verbatim including 'Three out of eighteen mice died on day 11', the pigmentation and autopsy sentences, MTD >1.5 g/kg and LD50 2 g/kg p.o. Sharma's XRF sentence is verbatim and my own check confirms the paper contains no ppm or concentration values and no toxicity or contaminant testing of the finished product. Rules 4, 5, 6, 8 and 9 are satisfied: doseLimits discloses species, oral route, per-kg-of-mouse basis and single-dose nature in-field; pregnancy and lactation are 'avoid'; no study arms are spliced; no efficacy, comparator or indication appears outside bibliographic titles; every hazard raised has a matching entry.

audit: VERDICT: reject. All three previously blocking defects are fixed at the root and I re-verified each against the live sources. The record is now close, and the great bulk of it is exactly right. It fails on three statements the record makes ABOUT ITS SOURCES that do not survive checking, one of which is an invented methodological limitation contradicted by a figure in the very paper the record leans on hardest.

audit: BLOCKING 1 (Rule 2, invented methodological detail). heavyMetals states: "as reported here EDAX identifies elements only, giving no concentration and no chemical species, so the chromium, manganese and zinc it lists are unquantified and unspeciated." The first clause is false. Tripathi 2013's EDAX report is Figure 2 (graphic ASL-32-199-g003.jpg, retrievable at https://cdn.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/blobs/6ba6/4078469/d681c40ee938/ASL-32-199-g003.jpg), and it is a quantitative EDAX/AMETEK Microanalysis Report prepared at IIT-Roorkee dated 6/24/2008 carrying an Element / Wt% / At% table: C 04.88/08.68, O 38.59/51.50, Na 01.61/01.50, Mg 01.94/01.71, Al 15.11/11.96, Si 23.28/17.70, S 04.39/02.93, K 00.85/00.47, Fe 09.33/03.57, Matrix Correction ZAF. So EDAX as reported here DOES give concentrations, for nine elements. The rebuilder opened Table 4's image but evidently not Figure 2's, and then asserted a reporting limitation the paper does not have. Root fix: state what is actually checkable, which happens to support the same conclusion more strongly. The paper's narrative lists thirteen elements (C, O, Na, Mg, Al, Si, S, K, Fe, B, Cr, Mn and Zn) while its own EDAX report tabulates Wt% and At% for only nine (C, O, Na, Mg, Al, Si, S, K, Fe); boron, chromium, manganese and zinc appear in the narrative list but in no quantified table anywhere in the paper, so those four remain unquantified, and EDAX gives no chemical species for any element. Keep the Cr/Mn/Zn conclusion; delete the false general clause.

audit: REJECT on a single defect, but it is squarely in the Rule 11 family this record has now been rejected for twice: an unverifiable negative asserted about the contents of a source the record itself says it could not read. insufficientReason states, of PMC3331427, 'The PDF full text could not be retrieved from the permitted host during this check, so no claim is made here about its contents beyond the HTML record.' Eight sentences later it states 'Across all eight, none reports for Vatagajankusha Rasa an elemental assay, a quantitative composition, a dose, an interaction, a contraindication, or any adverse-event, pregnancy or lactation datum.' Those two sentences cannot both be true of what the record did. The same field also opens the per-article section with 'What each of the eight actually contains, checked by fetching each article', which is contradicted for one of the eight. I confirmed the retrieval failure myself and it is not the rebuilder's fault: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/instance/3331427/pdf/ASL-6-203.pdf and the www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov equivalent both return a 1.8 KB HTML interstitial carrying a proof-of-work challenge (POW_CHALLENGE / POW_DIFFICULTY 4 / cookie cloudpmc-viewer-pow), not the PDF. So the blanket negative does not reproduce for a reader following the record's own stated method, and PMC3331427 is a 1987 Ancient Science of Life article on Amavata in which the term match presumably lies in unread scanned text - exactly the kind of article that could carry a formulation name with a dose.

audit: Fix that would make this approvable, and nothing else needs to move: scope the summary sentence to what was actually read, e.g. 'Across the seven of the eight whose text could be read, none reports for Vatagajankusha Rasa an elemental assay, a quantitative composition, a dose, an interaction, a contraindication, or any adverse-event, pregnancy or lactation datum; the eighth, PMC3331427, is held only as a scanned PDF that could not be retrieved (the PMC PDF endpoint returns a proof-of-work interstitial), so nothing is asserted about its contents beyond its HTML abstract.' Correspondingly soften 'checked by fetching each article' to 'checked by fetching each article, except PMC3331427, whose PDF full text could not be retrieved'. The safety conclusion is unaffected: nothing in the record's grading rests on the unread PDF.
